title: The Testing Effect: Why Explaining Beats Re-Reading
explainer: Cognitive psychology research, especially a series of studies by Henry Roediger and Jeffrey Karpicke in the 2000s, found that actively retrieving information from memory — as when explaining a concept aloud or taking a practice quiz — produces much better long-term retention than passively re-reading the same material, even though retrieval feels harder and less comfortable in the moment. This "testing effect" is part of why teaching something to someone else is a genuine mechanism for deepening your own mastery, not just a way to demonstrate mastery you already have.
